id_and_class.summary: Claire Sergent argues that conscious access is delayed and can desynchronize from sensory input, so the brain can bring a stimulus into awareness ‘offline’, after it has gone, if it becomes relevant. She revises the global neuronal workspace model: sensory representations are first shared across a broad ‘global playground’ of brain areas, which turns into a full global workspace when a task recruits decision-making.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Temporally Flexible Global Access

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is conscious access: global sharing of information across brain networks, which need not follow the real-time order of external events.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Conscious access is a pattern of large-scale brain activity, as in the global neuronal workspace model it extends.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence, from information sharing among brain networks.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Distributed cortical networks, sensory representations held for several hundred milliseconds, and decision-making processes that recruit them.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Behavioral experiments on the timing of awareness, EEG, MEG, intracranial recordings and fMRI in healthy adults and patients with disorders of consciousness.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Two tiers: a global playground where sensory representations are shared and maintained with no specific agenda, and a global workspace formed when task-driven decision processes join it.

mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Offline conscious access: information held in the global playground can enter awareness later, when attention or relevance calls for it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Conscious access lags behind stimulation and can be triggered after a stimulus disappears, so experience need not mirror the sequence of events in the world.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: A broad network of brain areas among which sensory representations are shared, a subset of the global workspace.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Sergent suggests that the capacity to process information offline made conscious processing worth having despite its slowness and limited capacity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Information is integrated dynamically over time according to context and relevance.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Sensory representations are maintained for several hundred milliseconds in the playground, offering more cognitive options than automatic unconscious processing, and are broadcast more fully when a task demands it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Offline processing would have made sluggish, capacity-limited conscious access adaptive.
core_claims_and_evidence: In retro-perception, attention cued after a stimulus vanishes can trigger conscious perception of it.
Temporal flexibility of access helps explain the psychological refractory period, attentional blink, postdictive effects and iconic memory.
Covert conscious access depends on a global playground, which becomes a global workspace when decision-making is added.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical: experimental psychology and human electrophysiology.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Retro-cueing paradigms, attentional blink and refractory-period tasks, and studies of preconscious processing and working memory without consciousness.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent with the physicalist global neuronal workspace framework it revises.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since conscious access is a pattern of brain network activity, it ends with the brain.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The theory explains conscious access as an adaptive brain process.
